feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader with clear domain focus, solid progression, and relevant technical depth. It reads professionally and shows impact, but it would be stronger with tighter structure, more quantified outcomes beyond activity descriptions, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience align well around digital platform leadership, governance, analytics, and public-sector communications.  
- Strong credibility: long tenure at NACo with visible progression from coordinator to director supports seniority and trustworthiness.  
- Good impact signals: website scale, audience size, platform migration, analytics stack, and studio build-out give concrete evidence of scope.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities well but need sharper results (e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, cost savings, search performance).  
- Simplify and de-duplicate structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap; consolidating them would improve scannability.  
- Fix style consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma); “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”; footer project formatting may feel dense in plain-text CV parsing.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of scale or scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and reduce abstraction: replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct language.
- Add a scale marker from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Recast the second sentence to emphasize leadership outcomes, not just domains covered.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing public-sector communications platforms, governance, and content operations. Led enterprise web transformation for a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, while building analytics, editorial, multimedia, and AI-enabled systems that improve publishing efficiency and audience access.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Enterprise web modernization” and “analytics infrastructure” are repeated elsewhere; consider using one concrete example instead.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership capabilities will make it feel more distinct and polished.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and simplify wording for cleaner scanability.
- Replace “communications operations” with a more senior, strategic term like “communications leadership” or “channel operations.”
- Consider this version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space allows, prioritize the most differentiating items first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI-enabled search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” and “multimedia production” repeat language already used in the header and Recent Projects.
- This section also overlaps with Topline Skills; keep competencies broader and leave tools/platforms to the skills sections.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently reads like a repeat of the NACo experience section. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes, scope, or distinct formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro and make each item more concise, parallel, and scannable; e.g., “Selected recent projects:” followed by 4 short bullets.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed [project] to [business or user outcome].”
- Clarify specificity where possible: “legislative search,” “Drupal 10 microsite,” “10x20-foot conference installation,” “recurring advocacy video series.”
- Edit for style consistency: use “10 x 20-foot” (not “10×20-foot”), and consider “AI-powered” instead of “AI-enabled” if you want stronger, cleaner wording.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with recent NACo roles; avoid repeating the same wording from Work Experience.
- If space is tight, keep only the most differentiated projects (e.g., anniversary campaign and AI search).

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a dense task list and overlaps heavily with your 2022–2024 NACo leadership entry. Make it sharper by emphasizing what is new in this consulting phase, especially strategic advisory scope, AI search, and platform-specific outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + value: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and cross-channel content operations for its public-facing communications ecosystem.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and foreground outcomes: “Designed and improved workflows, analytics, and governance systems to strengthen organization-wide coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal work more concise: “Built campaign microsites, modular content components, and member-facing toolkits in Drupal; provided front-end implementation and CMS troubleshooting.”
- Keep one distinctive forward-looking bullet: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX.” Add metrics if available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance/workflows/analytics” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; frame this as advisory/optimization, not ownership.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections unless tied to a concrete project or result.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-value leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and distinguish director-level ownership from the earlier NACo roles focused on day-to-day operations and content production.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable outcomes where missing: growth in engagement, production savings from the studio, reporting speed, campaign performance, or workflow efficiency.
- Tighten channel bullet: replace “reaching tens of thousands” / “serving thousands” with exact subscriber/follower counts if available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “workflows,” and “digital operations” overlap with the current consultant role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video/programming language overlaps with the Associate Communications Director and Digital Media Manager roles; emphasize building the studio and scaling institutional capacity, not recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel growth, and editorial operations at that stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and level: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media, and video, supporting NACo’s advocacy messaging and cross-channel editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video contribution with impact if possible: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” Add views, cadence, or audience growth if available.
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with stronger ownership: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning/workflows” overlaps with the Director role’s governance/planning bullet.
- “Produced weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the channel.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and the most current strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording tied to recent work:  
- Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization  
- Editorial governance & content operations  
- Cross-channel communications leadership  
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging  
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Use “content operations” instead of “content planning” to better reflect governance/workflow leadership shown in recent roles.
- Add “platform modernization” to align with the 10,000+ page Drupal migration and current consulting work.
- Keep each line parallel in structure; avoid mixing nouns (“strategy”) with adjectives (“audience-focused”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communication.”
- “Editorial systems and governance” is close to “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture”; consider consolidating across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. Use this topline item to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to your NACo web modernization and AI search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put the most relevant/recent strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, API/workflow work.
- Cut lower-priority platforms unless central to target roles; consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here if they already appear in Technical + IT.
- If space allows, make outcomes implicit: “enterprise CMS modernization” and “search and discovery experiences” signal impact better than standalone nouns.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same platform list in both places.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies and Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list that aligns well with the 2022–present leadership roles, but it reads as a generic inventory. Tighten it to emphasize strategic use of analytics and decision support, not just platforms.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” rather than only product names.
- Group tools and outcomes: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery” + “KPI frameworks, executive dashboards, performance analysis.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger business language like “executive reporting” or “decision-ready dashboards.”
- Consider revised line: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI & BigQuery • KPI framework design • Executive dashboards & reporting • SEO, UX and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo Director bullet on analytics infrastructure; keep this section tool/capability-focused and leave impact/results to recent experience.
- If space is tight, “SEO and performance analysis” may be redundant with broader “digital performance analysis.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with the “Multimedia & live event production” competency plus multiple NACo experience bullets. Make it more specific, senior, and operations-focused rather than a basic task list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize delivery scope and leadership: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Virtual event production workflows”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “End-to-end video production” or “Broadcast-quality video production”
- Consider adding one higher-value capability instead of a basic one: “Run-of-show planning,” “Technical direction,” or “Studio buildout and operations”
- If space allows, align with recent impact: “In-house studio operations” ties directly to the 2022–2024 role and feels more distinctive than “studio operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with Core Competencies: “Multimedia & live event production”; avoid repeating the same wording
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” and “Livestreaming” are close; combine or differentiate them

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Since recent roles are strongly Drupal-centered, this item should either sharpen to platform depth/relevance or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light qualifiers only where defensible, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise content publishing, microsites)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, rename the heading to **CMS & Web Publishing Platforms** for clearer alignment with your experience.
- Keep this item platform-only; save implementation detail for the adjacent technical section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one instance or using this section for tools not named elsewhere.
- Avoid adding “CMS modernization” or coding terms here—they already appear in other skills sections.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools that support your recent Drupal, automation, and web operations work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript, API integrations, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) and keep formatting consistent: HTML • CSS • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- If space allows, group by function for readability: Front-end: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery | Web ops: GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions | Integrations: APIs
- If you can substantiate it elsewhere, add scope in a parenthetical: “used for CMS front-end implementation, tagging, automation, and deployment workflows”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- GTM may also fit under analytics/measurement rather than coding.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with stronger “workflow automation” positioning elsewhere. Make it more selective and grouped around systems you actively use to build/coordinate workflows.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a flat list to capability-led categories, e.g.: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Prioritize the most relevant tools first: keep Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana; consider dropping older/generic collaboration tools if space is tight.
- Use consistent naming: “Microsoft Teams” instead of “Teams.”
- If accurate, add a light qualifier for impact/level, e.g. “built workflow systems in Airtable and Power Automate” or “admin-level use” elsewhere in the CV rather than here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language verbatim.
- Slack/Teams are low-value if left uncontextualized; they can dilute stronger technical tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful category, but it reads as a bare software list and misses the strategic email/engagement strength shown in recent NACo roles. Tightening the label and adding one or two capability cues would make it feel more senior and relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Replace with: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Newsletter operations • Audience segmentation**
- If accurate, strengthen further with outcome-oriented capabilities instead of more tools: **Email campaign deployment • List segmentation • Journey automation**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one is older/light use, consider dropping it for focus.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel claims in Core Competencies; use this line specifically for email/CRM platform expertise.
- Avoid adding analytics terms here; those are already well covered in Topline Skills and recent experience.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and misses a chance to show level of use or business impact. Since recent roles already prove these platforms, this item should be tighter and more differentiated.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics & Optimization Tools**
- Tighten and group for readability: **GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI dashboarding**
- Replace generic “Dashboarding” with **KPI dashboarding** or **executive reporting dashboards** to sound more outcome-oriented.
- If space allows, add proficiency context tied to recent work: **Enterprise web analytics, behavior analysis, reporting, and optimization**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to **Topline Skills [3] Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider removing one version or making this one tools-only and the other outcomes-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already referenced in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating the full list elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful “first in-house digital team” context, but the bullet is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles on workflows, weekly video updates, and channel management. Make this entry more foundational and execution-focused.

Suggested edit
- Emphasize early-build contributions: “Promoted across two roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Replace generic phrases with concrete outputs: website refresh support, livestream production, recurring video series, junior staff guidance.
- If possible, add scale: number of livestreams/events, cadence of video updates, audience reach, or size of team supported.
- Suggested rewrite: “Promoted across two roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia production. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced livestreams and a recurring weekly video update, and helped formalize day-to-day publishing workflows. Provided informal supervision and training to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthening workflows” overlaps with 2018–2024 NACo entries; keep it lighter here.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears later; frame this as helping launch the series rather than leading/expanding it.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It should be tightened and framed as a foundation in digital/multimedia support rather than repeating broader digital leadership themes covered in later NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the strongest differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast…”
- Replace vague phrasing like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer support language tied to programs/policy.
- Keep scope modest and concise since later roles show greater leadership; emphasize execution, content production, and cross-team support.
- If possible, add outputs or reach (episodes produced, stakeholder groups supported, content volume).

Suggested rewrite
- Supported innovation and research initiatives for NACo program and policy teams, coordinating project deliverables and communications materials.
- Produced digital and multimedia content to support organizational programs, including writing, scripting, and asset development.
- Launched NACo’s first podcast, managing planning, scripting, recording coordination, and production.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic “digital content production” language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership here; save team-building and strategy language for later positions.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software, workflows, and production capabilities. It also overlaps with stronger, more recent multimedia leadership already shown elsewhere, so this item should stay concise and tool-focused.

Suggested edit:
